# Objective

The objective of this file is to create a data entry file to run the Biotic Ligand Model (BLM) desktop version for predicting Cu speciation (BLM_Data_Entry_for_Cu.xlsx) using the WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean.xlsx in the WaDE Data Cleaning folder.

The BLM_Data_Entry_for_Cu.xlsx file will be used to copy and paste data into BLM (desktop version) and run to obtain the output files located in Spatial Assessment of Bioavailability Project\Copper\\1. Running BLM\Data outputs.

The BLM requires the following variables to run with the following units:

-   Site Name

-   Sample Name

-   Temperature (C)

-   pH

-   Copper concentration (ug/L)

-   Dissolved organic carbon concentration (DOC mg C/L)

-   Humic acid (HA %)

-   Calcium concentration (Ca mg/L)

-   Magnesium concentration (Mg mg/L)

-   Sodium concentration (Na mg/L)

-   Potassium concentration (K mg/L)

-   Sulfate concentration (SO4 mg/L)

-   Chloride concentration (Cl mg/L)

-   Alkalinity as dissolved inorganic carbon concentration (DIC mg/L)

-   Sulfur concentration (S mg/L): under development, but must enter an arbitrary small quantity

We will be obtaining these variables from the WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Final.xlsx file.

# 1. Set working directory

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/Trace-element-bioavailability-spatial-assessment/Copper/1. Running BLM/Data inputs")
```

# 2. Import the clean WaDE Synoptic Summary dataset

```{r}
library(readxl)

WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/Trace-element-bioavailability-spatial-assessment/WaDE Dataset Cleaning/WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean.xlsx")

head(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean)
```

Inspect the structure

```{r}
str(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean)
```

# 3. Select BLM Input Variables

Select variables to create a BLM data entry file for running Cu in speciation mode:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(rlang)

# 1. Create a loop function to create a data frame for any BLM element of choice

create_blm_input <- function(df, metal){

  metal_sym <- sym(metal)

  df %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Sample_ID,
      Site,
      Temp_C,
      pH,
      !!metal_sym,
      DOC_uM,
      Ca_uM,
      Mg_uM,
      Na_uM,
      K_uM,
      SO4_uM,
      Cl_uM,
      DIC_uM
    )
}

# 2. Run it for the following trace elements
cu_blm_input_df <- create_blm_input(WaDE_Synoptic_Summary_Clean, "Cu_uM")

# 3. Check the results
head(cu_blm_input_df)
```

Add a column for humic acid at 10 % after DOC

```{r}
library(dplyr)

cu_blm_input_df <- cu_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(
    HA = 10 ) %>%
  relocate(HA, .after = DOC_uM)

# Check
head(cu_blm_input_df)
```

Add a column for S at the end, set to a negligible amount since BLM requires this input

```{r}
library(dplyr)

cu_blm_input_df <- cu_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate('S_uM' = 1e-10)

# Check
summary(cu_blm_input_df$S_uM)
```

# 4. Unit Conversions

Convert and rewrite trace element units from uM to ug/L

```{r}
library(dplyr)

cu_blm_input_df <- cu_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(Cu_uM = Cu_uM * 63.546) %>% # Overwrite Zn (uM) with Zn (ug/L) value
  rename(Cu_ug_L = Cu_uM) # rename AFTER overwriting

# Check
str(cu_blm_input_df)
```

Convert DOC, Ca, Mg, Na, K, Cl, SO4, and S from uM to mg/L

```{r}
library(dplyr)

cu_blm_input_df <- cu_blm_input_df %>%
  mutate(
    DOC_uM = DOC_uM * 12.01e-3,
    Ca_uM  = Ca_uM  * 40.078e-3,
    Mg_uM  = Mg_uM  * 24.305e-3,
    Na_uM  = Na_uM  * 22.990e-3,
    K_uM   = K_uM   * 39.098e-3,
    Cl_uM  = Cl_uM  * 35.45e-3,
    SO4_uM = SO4_uM * 96.06e-3,
    S_uM   = S_uM   * 32.06e-3
  ) %>%
  rename(
    DOC_mg_L = DOC_uM,
    Ca_mg_L  = Ca_uM,
    Mg_mg_L  = Mg_uM,
    Na_mg_L  = Na_uM,
    K_mg_L   = K_uM,
    Cl_mg_L  = Cl_uM,
    SO4_mg_L = SO4_uM,
    S_mg_L   = S_uM
  )

# Check
str(cu_blm_input_df)
```

## 5. Export to Excel

```{r}
library(writexl)

write_xlsx(cu_blm_input_df, "BLM_Data_Entry_for_Cu.xlsx")
```
